notes.title: Unstuck Update
notes.content:
We’ve been gathering feedback and analyzing data over the past few months. The feedback has been overwhelmingly positive, for which we are very grateful. However, our data has revealed a slight issue: the game is too difficult. While we intended for the game to be challenging, it appears we might have overdone it.

Currently, only about 30% of players make it past B9 (halfway through the game), and only 5% manage to finish the game. Some levels are particularly easy to get stuck on, and since there aren't many ways to progress, getting stuck usually means game over. We wanted to address this issue and offer more paths forward. [b]Here’s what we’ve done:[/b]

[list]
[*] Dropped hints across the more challenging production lines
[*] Completely redesigned the level unlocking system, making it non-linear (see screenshot)
[*] Added 6 practice levels to the B set to provide useful insights
[/list]

[b]Additionally, this update includes:[/b]

[list]
[*] 2 bonus levels (AZ, BZ)
[*] 3 new achievements
[*] More animations
[/list]

If you’re stuck, update the game and see if it helps. If you’re not stuck, congratulations! And if you haven’t gotten the game yet, it will be on sale soon!

Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Inside the Procedural Soundtrack
First patch
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Added controller support (experimental for now; the default mapping may change)
[*] Improved game- and level-loading speed (level transitions should be smooth now)
[*] Tutorial texts can now be disabled in the settings (at your own risk)
[*] Benchmark level does not grant achievements anymore
[*] In comparison, the full game now grants achievements for progress in the demo
[*] The dates of saved solutions are now displayed in local time instead of UTC
[*] The outline of the selected Input gate now renders correctly
[*] Enhanced UI for keyboard and controller and minor UI improvements
[*] Minor changes in tutorial and hints
[/list]

notes.title: Omnibullet is now available!
notes.content:
After more than 3 years of development, we are finally releasing Omnibullet. What started as a semestral project of three IT students is now a full-scale indie game with over 30 hours of playtime, dozens of levels, and a merciless difficulty curve.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43082568/e72be64af70c2c9c920077442f9024e2ba91465e.png[/img]

Ommibullet was developed with almost zero budget. Not counting our time, the only costs were the domain hosting and the Steam entry fee. Instead of doing marketing and other meta stuff, we have invested our energy into development, polishing, and delivering the best possible game to those of you who gave Omnibullet a shot, played the demo, or just wishlisted it, despite it being a very obscure game. 

If you decide to purchase the full version, we hope that we are delivering what you came for. If you like the game, please, consider writing a review as it can help tremendously with Steam visibility. If something does not work properly, or you just want to talk to us, join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/eMrBhKQses]discord server[/url] and let us know.

Thank you all for your support. 

[h3]Release notes for the full game[/h3]
- there are now two leaderboards for each production line: one that contains all achieved scores (for all those minmaxers amongst you) and one that only contains scores achieved without refunding used towers (elegant solutions)
- solutions can now be saved and loaded (no need to rebuild the entire system upon return)
- it is now possible to control the game using the keyboard or gamepad (this is still experimental and will be improved in the first patch)
- several tutorial changes

[h3]Shorter demo[/h3]
Since its release, the demo contained 12 levels (A0-A9, B0, B1). However, we have noticed that over 80 % of players would finish the A9 level and then stop playing. This is likely caused by A9 seeming like a natural end, and since players did not know, they could continue with the B set, they closed the game without ever seeing the final demonstration level showcasing the features of the full game. To address this, we have decided to cut the demo. The last demo level is no A7 and when the player clicks on A8, they will be presented with the final demonstration level and the demo version will end. 

Thanks for reading.

notes.title: Omnibullet is ready for Next Fest! New demo is out.
notes.content:
What is new:
[list]
[*] Scores and leaderboards: when you solve a level, you will obtain a score based on several metrics. This score is then visible in the leaderboards so that you can see how well you did.
[*] Czech translations: the game is now completely localized into Czech (can be changed in the settings)
[*] Brand new UI (no more gray buttons, towers have icons now)
[*] Advanced tower placement mode: multiple towers can now be placed at once (activate in the settings)
[*] Even less text in tutorials: learn by doing, not by reading
[*] Improved lighting
[*] Steam integrations (Steam overlay in the demo; Statistics and Achievements in the full game)
[*] Minor visual improvements
[/list]

What is coming soon:
[list]
[*] Saving and loading solutions for specific levels
[*] Release 
[/list]

notes.title: Demo is out and Devlog is on!
notes.content:
Hello! As the title suggests, we have released a demo version where you can try out the first line of levels (and a bit) and learn how to design systems for charging batteries. You can play the game on Windows and, as we've heard, possibly even on Steamdeck. None of the developers owns it, though, so we haven't tested that option. We will appreciate any feedback, be it technical or related to the game content. Please let us know!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43082568/d216bd8274943d5070078fd28a9a41b346702b27.jpg[/img]

In other news, we have started publishing a devlog, which you can check out at [url=https://omnibullet.cz/devlog/]omnibullet.cz/devlog/[/url]. Some posts discuss technical highlights from the development, and others bring general status updates and sneak peeks of upcoming improvements. Since we only work on the game in our spare time, we post rather irregularly, but hopefully, that won't deter you from reading.

Thanks to everyone who has added the game to their wishlists! It means a lot to us and helps the game move forward.
